$comment: D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-WITH-STORAGE-CLASS (TF-C77), MODE 2: a GNU attribute in the MID position, between the type head and the declarator list — the `declAttrRun` slot. Covers the literal sqlite function-definition shape (`static int __attribute__((cold)) sf(int x){…}`, the MODE-2 position, 20 of sqlite's 119 SQLITE_NOINLINE sites — 16 × `static T SQLITE_NOINLINE f(` + 4 × `T SQLITE_NOINLINE f(`; the census counts `.c` files ONLY, splitting 119 as 90/9/16/4 over mode 3 / leading / the two mode-2 shapes, and including the 3 `.h` prototype sites gives 122 = 90/10/16/6, i.e. 22 in mode 2. The figure 99 belongs to MODE 3 (90 plus the 9 leading sites), which is the dominant sqlite position but NOT the one this example exercises), a mid-position `weak` object resolved across a real cross-TU link, and a mid-position `aligned(64)` gated on the RUNTIME ADDRESS. MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD all three were a hard `error[P0009] expected 'Identifier', 'ParenOpen', 'StarOp', 'EndStatement', 'BracketOpen' or 'BlockOpen' — got '__attribute__'`. ★★ THE GRAMMAR AND THE ENGINE CHANGE ARE ONE UNIT, AND THIS EXAMPLE WITNESSES BOTH HALVES INDEPENDENTLY. Two separate keys carry the slot to two separate sinks: `declarationAttrSlotRules` → the semantic attribute scan → `aligned`; `linkagePrefixRoots`'s slot roots → the HIR linkage fold → `weak`. Either one missing is a SILENT drop, and they break DIFFERENT checks. NON-VACUITY PROVEN PER CHECK against the FINAL build, isolated into its own program and built four ways — as written / `declarationAttrSlotRules` removed (H1) / `linkagePrefixRoots` reverted to prefix-only (H2) / the row indices left at their pre-TF-C77 values (H3): row 1 (&av % 64) = 42 / 1-SILENT / 42 / COMPILE-ERR; row 2 (wd == 5) = 42 / LINK dup sym / LINK dup sym / COMPILE-ERR; row 3 (sf(41) == 42) = 42 / 42 / 42 / COMPILE-ERR. The H1 cell on row 1 is the important one: the program still COMPILES AND LINKS with ZERO diagnostics of any code and simply returns the wrong number — that is the silent-drop state this cycle exists to make impossible. Running H1 and H2 separately (rather than one whole-file revert) is what proves the two changes are genuinely independent halves. ★★ THE OFFSET BREAKER `data_pad` IS LOAD-BEARING and must be the SAME SECTION CLASS as the over-aligned object it precedes; DO NOT delete it, and do not add an over-aligned global without one. This was MEASURED the hard way during authoring: an UNINITIALIZED `char pad;` (.bss) in front of an INITIALIZED `av` (.data) left the alignment check returning 42 even under H1, i.e. VACUOUS, because the first over-aligned global in a section lands at a page-aligned section start. An initialized `data_pad = 1` makes the natural placement differ from the aligned placement, and RE-MEASURED the check then reads 42 → 1 under H1. ★ Row 3 is a COMPILE-GATE witness and cu_a.c says so rather than pretending otherwise — `cold` is an ABI-neutral hint with no runtime effect, so no exit code can move on it; it is here because the regression it guards IS a compile failure (that is exactly how the P0009 presented) and because it is the position sqlite actually uses. It also pins the `kindByChild` index move [2,0] → [3,0]: leave that behind and the definition is mis-lowered as a variable and the file does not compile. The TU also carries a DECLARATOR-LESS declaration (`struct P { int x; };`), the index shape where the optional init-declarator list is ABSENT and the role children are one shorter — exactly where a hand-moved index goes wrong. ★ The mid-position binding is DECLARATION-level, not per-declarator, and that is C semantics rather than convention: GROUND TRUTH IS REAL CLANG, MEASURED with `clang -c` + `nm -m`, `int __attribute__((weak)) ma = 1, mb = 2;` emits BOTH as 'weak external' — contrast the AFTER-DECLARATOR run pinned in examples/c-subset/gnu_attribute_linkage_positions_crosscu/, where only the declarator it follows is weak. The `release` arm is MANDATORY, not decoration: the point is witnessing that the real SHIPPED optimizer PRESERVES both the alignment and the weak binding rather than re-laying-out the globals or inlining through the weak symbol. The whole example is VERIFIED clang-clean over BOTH CUs (`-fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -isysroot $(xcrun --show-sdk-path)`, zero errors, zero warnings) and the clang-linked two-CU binary independently exits 42, so the expected exit code is ground truth from a real toolchain — a corpus example must witness REAL C, not merely C that DSS happens to accept.
